questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and make a grammatically correct sentence.

I wasn’t feeling well yesterday, but I feel a little ________ today.
questions.solution:
The correct solution is option 3.

The word 'better' is grammatically correct because 'better' is in the comparative degree.

Here, a comparison is made between the condition of someone's health on the previous day and the present day.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

ABANDONED
questions.solution:
The correct solution is option 4.

'Abandoned' means having been deserted or left.

So, the most appropriate synonym of 'Abandoned' is 'Deserted', which means (of a place) empty of people.

Let us look into the meaning of other words:

 
• 'Continued' means without a break in continuity; ongoing.
 
• 'Initiated' means cause (a process or action) to begin.
 
• 'Adopted' means legally take (another's a child) and bring it up as one's own.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the word.

APPLAUD
questions.solution:
The correct solution is option 3.

'Applaud' means show approval or praise by clapping.

So, the most appropriate antonym of 'Applaud' is 'Criticize', which means indicate the faults of (someone or something) in a disapproving way.

Let us look into the meaning of other words:

 
• 'Praise' means express warm approval or admiration of.
 
• 'Clap' means strike the palms of (one's hands) together repeatedly, typically in order to applaud someone or something.
 
• 'Cheer' means shout for joy or in praise or encouragement.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

An animal that lives by killing and eating other animals
questions.solution:
The correct solution is option 4.

'Predator' means an animal that naturally preys on others.

So, the most appropriate word for the given group of words is 'Predator'. 

Let us look into the meaning of other words:

• 'Prey' means an animal that is hunted and killed by another for food.

questions.question:

questions.question:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.

After a heated argument, they went to their respective place.
questions.solution:
The correct solution is option 1.

'respective place' is grammatically wrong because the subject is 'they' which is plural. So, the correct word must be 'places'.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No. 1.
questions.solution:
The correct solution is option 1.

'observed' is grammatically correct because it means to notice or perceive (something) and register it as being significant.

Here, people are in wonder about the bird's flight by observing them fly. So, 'observed' is the correct word.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No. 2.
questions.solution:
The correct solution is option 1.

'Their' is grammatically correct because it means belonging to or associated with the people or things previously mentioned or easily identified.

Here, birds are already mentioned and further their songs are also mentioned. So, 'their' (used for plural nouns) is correct.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No. 3.
questions.solution:
The correct solution is option 2.

'Unique' means to be the only one of its kind; unlike anything else.

Not all birds are the same. So, in the form of a group, they are unique.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No. 4.
questions.solution:
The correct solution is option 4.

'With' means accompanied by (another person or thing).

Feathers are on their body. In other words, we can say they are covered with feathers.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No. 5.
questions.solution:
The correct solution is option 1.

'separates' means to divide into constituent or distinct elements or cause to move or be apart.

Here, the sentence is in the simple present tense. So, 'separates' is correct as the subject 'evolutionary development' is singular.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the word.

Congested
questions.solution:
The correct solution is "cleared".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **'Congested**' means crowded with traffic or people as to hinder or prevent freedom of movement.

 
 
• **Example** - Traffic still gets **congested **because of the bridge construction.
 
 
 
• **'Cleared'** means getting rid of objects or obstructions.
 
 
• **Example **-Someone had **carefully** cleared the area.
 
 
 
• So, the most appropriate antonym of **'congested**' is **'cleared**'.

​Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **'Choked' **means having severe difficulty in breathing because of a constricted or obstructed throat or a lack of air.

 
 
• **Example** - He **choked** back his tears.
 
 
 
• '**Crammed'** means completely fill (a place or container) to the point of overflowing.
 
 
• **Example** - He **crammed** the suitcase with his clothes.
 
 

 
• **'Crowded'** means full of people, leaving little or no room for movement; packed.

 
 
• **Example** - The street was **crowded** and noisy.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

A large crowd of people intent on causing trouble or violence
questions.solution:
The correct solution is "Mob".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• '**Mob**' means a large crowd of people, especially one that is disorderly and intent on causing trouble or violence.

 
 
• **Example** - The angry** mob** smashed store windows and attacked people on the streets. 
 
 
 
• So, the most appropriate word for the given group of words is 'mob'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• Let us look into the meaning of other words:
 
 
• '**Audience**' means the assembled spectators or listeners at a public event such as a play, film, concert, or meeting.

 
 
• Example - The concert **attracted** a large audience. 
 
 
 
• '**Spectators**' means a person who watches a game or another event.
 
 
• Example - The **spectators** lining the road cheered the racers on. 
 
 
 
• '**Procession**' means many people or vehicles moving forward in an orderly fashion, especially as part of a ceremony.
 
 
• Example - Huge crowds followed the funeral** procession** in a public demonstration of grief.

questions.question:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No Error'.

Sushmita’s youngest sister is not only beautiful but even intelligent also.
questions.solution:
The correct solution is option 2.

'not only.... but also' is grammatically correct. 

In the given sentence, 'even.. also' is given, which is grammatically wrong.

__Correct sentence:__ *Sushmita’s youngest sister is not only beautiful but also intelligent.*

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement

While the teacher was scrutinizing the sums, Swaminathan was __gazing on__ his face.
questions.solution:
The correct solution is option 2.

'gazing at' is grammatically correct because 'at' is used to express location or arrival in a particular place or position.

So, 'on' is grammatically wrong because it means to be physically in contact with and supported by (a surface). 

The correct preposition that follows *gaze* is *at*. Example - *to gaze **at **the scenery.*

questions.question:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.

Ram cannot withdraw all his money unless he does not give a prior notice.
questions.solution:
**The correct solution is option 4.**

'unless he does not give' is grammatically incorrect because 'unless' means except if.

Here, 'unless' and 'does not' are contrary to each other. So, it's wrong. 

__Correct sentence__: *Ram cannot withdraw all his money **if** he does not give prior notice.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__***

 
• “if” is conditional. It is used to describe a possible situation, and what would happen under the conditions of that situation
 
 
• **For E.g.-** "**If **you don't save some money, you can't go on vacation
 
 
 
• “Unless” is also conditional, but it is effectively “if” with an extra exclusion or negative qualifier added
 
 
• **For e.g.-** You can't go on vacation **unless** you save some money.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank and make a meaningful sentence.

Winning both the races has been a ________ surprise, but the success is well deserved.
questions.solution:
The correct solution is option 1.

The word 'pleasant' means giving a sense of happy satisfaction or enjoyment.

'Civilized' means at an advanced stage of social and cultural development.

'Charming' means very pleasant or attractive.

Winning always gives a sense of happiness. So, 'pleasant' is the correct word.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and make a grammatically correct sentence.

If I ________ that you were coming over, I would have cancelled my programme.
questions.solution:
The correct solution is option 1.

'had known' is the correct answer because 'had' is used for the past perfect tense. 

The past perfect tense is used when we are talking about the past and want to refer back to an earlier past time.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement

A little carefulness __can have averted__ the accident.
questions.solution:
**The correct solution is option 1.**

'could' is the correct word because it can be used when a condition must be fulfilled for the thing to happen.

'Can' is used when there is nothing that would stop the thing from happening

So, the correct word must be 'could have averted'.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

No strings attached

options.text: Involving a choice to be made

questions.solution:
**The correct solution is option 1.**

'No strings attached' refers to the act of doing something without asking for anything in return. 

So, the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom is 'Without conditions or restrictions'.

Example: “Danny said he'd do your chores today, no strings attached!”
